thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: sudden error-rate increase in routing path `kv-reuse` (service: inference-runtime) — 5xx spike, memory pressure on gpu-pool-2. Thresholds triggered at 2026-03-15T10:02:01Z

oncall-alex: Acked. I’m on it. Adding folks: @sam @li @nate. Paging customer SREs.

sam: seeing large KV cache growth and continuous-batching latency cliffs on p99. memory RSS on runtimes jumping from ~8GB -> 22GB in minutes.

li: adding telemetry: `kv_cache.entries_total` jumped 18x at ~10:01 UTC. Heap churn + GC spikes.

nate: also noticing request traces with mismatched seq offsets — some requests reusing KV frames from previous sessions. likely stale keys being returned.

customer-sre-jen: we have a customer reporting degraded responses (~20% timeouts) — they’re on Dedicated. I’ve opened a support ticket and flagged as P0 for them.

oncall-alex: collecting quick mitigations. Sam, can we toggle kv-reuse off for the affected pool?

sam: yeah. I’m preparing a hotfix toggle. Plan: (1) disable KV reuse on gpu-pool-2 (2) roll batch size down to baseline (3) revert aggressive prefix caching change from last deploy.

li: config snippet to flip: 
```yaml
service.runtime.pool_filters: ["gpu-pool-2"]
features.kv_reuse.enabled: false
batching.max_batch_tokens: 512
```
I’ll push as a config patch to the control plane.

nate: logs show one problematic path where `seq_offset` from request A is being left in the cache context and applied to request B. Example trace id: trace-87342. snippet: `kv.lookup(seq_offset=120) -> matched->applied to req 87342-B`.

oncall-alex: that explains cross-request leakage. Could be a race in cache GC or a reuse map key bug. Either way, disable kv_reuse ASAP.

sam: patch posted to canary, rolling to gpu-pool-2 now. deploy-bot: `deploy 2026-03-15_hotfix/kv-reuse-disable` started.

deploy-bot: Canary success: 3/3 hosts. Proceeding to remainder of pool.

sam: completed. kv_reuse toggled off for gpu-pool-2 at 2026-03-15T10:12:44Z. Observability: entries_total stabilized, mem usage trending down.

li: p95 latency improving, p99 still elevated but trending. error-rate dropped from 9.4% -> 1.8% in 6 minutes.

customer-sre-jen: customer confirms timeouts dropping. They want root cause and ETA for full fix.

sre-manager: Good quick mitigation. Next: need RCA loop — is this a regression from last week’s batching optimizer? Who owns cache reuse correctness?

nate: I’ll take lead on root cause. Early hypothesis: reuse key derivation includes per-request `seq_offset` but we canonicalize keys incorrectly when batching boundaries overlap. Under high continuous-batching loads the reuse map returns entries with stale offsets. I can reproduce locally with a micro-benchmark.

oncall-alex: capture a snapshot of affected hosts for postmortem: /var/log/inference/kv_debug.log and runtime heap profiles. Sam, can you collect heapdumps and attach to the ticket?

sam: grabbing heapdumps now. saving to s3://incidents/2645000001/ and attaching. Also captured kernel OOM warnings? none, just process-level OOM handling.

product-oncall: we should assess customer impact window. Jen, can you confirm earliest observed customer error time + duration?

customer-sre-jen: earliest at ~10:00 UTC, degraded until 10:15 when mitigation active. Impact window ~15m. Affected customers: ACCT-992 (high), ACCT-331 (low). Documented in ticket INC-2645.

security-bot: Note: no signs of data exfil or auth failures. All errors appear internal.

nate: reproducer notes:
- trigger: sustained high QPS with continuous-batching enabled and batch-slicing enabled
- observed: reuse_map key computed as `model_id|prefix_hash|batch_slice` but batch_slice used mutable `seq_offset` that changes during lifecycle
- consequence: later requests matched older entries whose `kv.seq_offset` didn't match request's own offset -> returned stale KV values

nate: minimal fix: ensure `seq_offset` is not part of reuse key OR include immutable request fingerprint. Longer-term: add strict validation of `seq_offset` at lookup time (if mismatch -> miss and eviction).

li: I suggest hotfix: 1) keep kv_reuse disabled until we ship a correctness patch; 2) revert batching optimizer flag that increases batch slice concurrency; 3) add a runtime check that asserts seq_offset equality at lookup to fail closed.

oncall-alex: approved. Sam, can we keep kv_reuse off until patch lands?

sam: yes. I’ve flagged it in control plane as disabled globally for affected regions. Will schedule safe-window deploy for correctness patch.

deploy-bot: created change request `CR-2645-kv-seq-check` targeting 2026-03-16 04:00 UTC for low-risk window.

customer-sre-jen: Thanks — customer wants timeline and whether any data corruption occurred. Any evidence of persisted bad state?

nate: no persisted corruption observed. This was in-memory reuse; once reuse disabled, subsequent requests allocate fresh contexts and returns are correct. No persisted keys mutated.

sre-manager: Action items:
- Nate: own RCA and PR for seq_offset validation (postmortem: root-cause + diff)
- Sam: monitor and keep kv_reuse disabled until patch verified
- Li: add alert for reuse_map.seq_mismatch_rate and `kv_cache.entries_total` anomaly rule
- Jen: update customer support ticket with mitigation summary and next steps

product-oncall: Also capture impact on billing/throughput — we saw ~12% cost bump when kv_reuse disabled; log that for customer communications.

oncall-alex: Handoff to night oncall in 40m. I’ll prepare a short pager with current status: mitigation applied, kv_reuse off, patch in review, customer notified, monitoring OK.

nate: PR opened: https://git.redwood/repo/infra/PR-8712 — adds seq_offset guard and unit tests + integration test. Requesting review from @li and @sam.

li: reviewed, leaving minor comments. adding an integration test to simulate overlapping batch slices.

sam: merging after li's test. Once merged we can enable kv_reuse behind a feature flag with stricter validation.

oncall-alex: Thanks all. Final note for postmortem: include timeline, why canary didn’t catch this (canary config used lower batch concurrency), and preventative work (static analysis on key derivation and stronger canary scenarios).

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: error-rate returned to baseline and memory reclaimed. severity: sev3 (customer impact tiered, P0 customer affected briefly). Postmortem requested.

sre-manager: Good containment. Nate, please file the postmortem doc and tag for review. I’ll schedule a blameless review next week.

customer-sre-jen: Customer updated. They appreciate the quick mitigation and want follow-up once a permanent fix is deployed.

oncall-alex: Handoff complete. Leaving notes in the incident channel. Night oncall, ping me if anything regresses.

sam: attaching heapdump link and quick perf graphs: s3://incidents/2645000001/heapdumps/, dashboard: https://dash.redwood/board/kv-cache-2645

nate: adding final note: root cause appears to be a correctness regression introduced when we optimized `batch_slice` reuse key composition. The fix is small but correctness-critical.

li: closing monitoring loop. Will add alert thresholds and unit tests in core.

product-oncall: postmortem owners assigned. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
